Fix :$var shorthand attributes breaking Blade's ComponentTagCompiler

ComponentNode::render() was expanding :$title into :$title="$title",
which is not valid Blade syntax. Blade's ComponentTagCompiler could not
parse the opening tag, leaving it uncompiled while still compiling the
closing tag — producing an orphaned endif and a ParseError.

Render :$var shorthand as-is without appending ="value".

Fix infinite loop in Blade compilation caused by null directive callback return

The callbacks in Directives::get() and Directives::has() had no return
statement, implicitly returning null. This null propagated through
BladeCompiler::compileStatements() → replaceFirstStatement(), where
strlen(null) evaluated to 0, preventing the offset from advancing and
causing an infinite loop during view compilation.

Co-authored-by: Filip Ganyicz <ganyicz.filip@gmail.com>

Bind `$this` in compiled functions when `@assets` directive is used

The `@endassets` directive checks `isset($this)` to determine whether
to store assets in the Livewire component store or the non-Livewire
fallback. Blaze wraps component templates in plain functions and only
binds `$this` via `Closure::bind()` when it detects the template needs
it. The detection checked for `$this`, `@entangle`, and `@script` but
not `@assets`, so `$this` was never available and assets always fell
through to `$nonLivewireAssets`. This caused assets to be missing from
Livewire AJAX responses (e.g. lazy-loaded or dynamically rendered
components).

fix: add file_exists check to ensureCompiled in-memory cache guard (#97)

The in-memory cache in ensureCompiled() assumed that once a view was
compiled, the compiled file would always exist on disk. When compiled
views are cleared (e.g. via artisan view:clear) while the process is
still running, the stale cache entry causes require_once to fail with
a file-not-found error.

Adding a file_exists($compiledPath) check alongside the isset() guard
ensures the compiled file is re-created when it has been removed.

Optimize BlazeAttributeBag constructor (#152)

Override the parent ComponentAttributeBag constructor to skip the
redundant setAttributes() check. The parent constructor calls
setAttributes() which checks if $attributes['attributes'] is an
instanceof ComponentAttributeBag — but in the Blaze path this is
always false because the Wrapper boilerplate already handles that
case before sanitized() is called.

This eliminates an isset() + instanceof check on every
BlazeAttributeBag instantiation (at least once per component render
via sanitized(), and again for every merge()/filter()/class() call).

when there are only two possible values (default and current).

Reduce per-call overhead for self-closing components (#162)

* Reduce per-call overhead for self-closing components

Use function_exists() guard instead of calling ensureRequired() on every
render. After the first render, function_exists() is a C-level check
that's faster than a PHP method call + hash table lookup.

Also adds a test verifying that self-closing components correctly
propagate data to @aware descendants via the data stack.

* Use function_exists() guard inside ensureRequired

Move the function_exists() check into ensureRequired() so both the
compiled caller and resolve() benefit from the C-level guard. Drop
the $required hash table which is now redundant.
